summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 12, part 81) in which Caroline Enderby, drugged and held in a private asylum-like house under the name Muriel Quelton, confesses to her friend Lexy how she was trapped. She describes Dr. Quelton's insistence that she is Muriel, the sale of a stolen emerald, and her growing attachment to Captain Grey, whom she had been expected to marry or leave behind. Captain Grey overhears part of the conversation from outside the door.
one_line: Caroline Enderby confesses to Lexy how Dr. Quelton held her under the name Muriel Quelton, and how Captain Grey overhears her.
key_facts: Caroline tells Lexy that the nurse kept calling her 'Mrs. Quelton' and that she insisted she was Caroline Enderby.
Dr. Quelton told Caroline: 'If you insist that you are Caroline Enderby, you're mad, and I'll send you to an asylum.'
Caroline says she was afraid of Dr. Quelton and did not dare tell Lexy the truth when Lexy visited that morning.
Caroline hoped Lexy would find the handkerchief and understand the situation.
Caroline says Captain Grey sat with her and that she had never known anyone like him.
Caroline had promised to marry Charles but says she cannot do so now.
Caroline says George told her that his wife had died a few months earlier and had left a jewel to her brother.
Lexy corrects Caroline, stating the jewel was an emerald, not a ruby.
George says Dr. Quelton had taken the emerald long ago and sold it to pay for his drugs.
Dr. Quelton's lawyer was never told that his sister had died, according to George's account.
Dr. Quelton said: 'Consequently, Muriel Quelton had to be here, and she was; and she'll remain here until her purpose is served!'
George says that once he learned Captain Grey was coming, he began looking for someone to take his wife's place.
Captain Grey was standing motionless outside the door and overheard Caroline's remarks about him.
Lexy sternly interrupts Caroline's remarks about Captain Grey's face and tells her to explain how she escaped.
